items.headline: Clippers, Steve Ballmer Accept NBA Penalties in Kawhi Leonard Salary Cap Circumvention Case
items.summary: Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer has publicly accepted the NBA's sweeping punishment for salary cap circumvention involving Kawhi Leonard. The penalties include a one-year ban for Ballmer, a $30 million fine for the team, and the forfeiture of five first-round draft picks. Ballmer expressed regret and stated the team is committed to moving past this chapter.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Trade to Raptors in Limbo Amid Clippers' Interim Governor Search
items.summary: The trade sending Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors remains unofficial nearly two weeks after the NBA's ruling against the Clippers. The deal is being held up as the Clippers have yet to appoint an interim governor to oversee front office operations, including trades, following the suspensions of key personnel, including owner Steve Ballmer and President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank.

items.headline: Jaylen Brown and LeBron James Join Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers made significant offseason moves, acquiring five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics on July 6, 2026, in exchange for Paul George and multiple draft picks. A few weeks later, the Sixers bolstered their roster further by signing LeBron James to a two-year contract in free agency, forming a formidable new 'super-user' core alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

items.headline: Jonathan Kuminga Chooses Timberwolves for Fit and Connection
items.summary: Forward Jonathan Kuminga has reportedly chosen to join the Minnesota Timberwolves. His decision was influenced by the strong on-court fit and genuine connections he felt with the team, including regular calls from star guards LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards, despite potentially being able to earn more elsewhere.

items.headline: Lakers Eyeing Paint Anchor Amid Roster Overhaul
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are reportedly in search of a proven paint anchor to bolster their frontcourt depth, especially after Mark Williams' injury. With 16 players currently on the roster, the Lakers may look for a two-for-one trade to trim their count and address their center needs.

items.headline: Pistons Eyeing Trade Market to Fill Roster Needs
items.summary: The Detroit Pistons, despite ongoing contract negotiations with Jalen Duren, are reportedly exploring the trade market. With several teams having holes to fill, the Pistons could have various options for making a significant deal to improve their roster.

items.headline: Jalen Duren's Contract Standoff with Pistons Continues
items.summary: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren is reportedly considering taking a qualifying offer if the team doesn't meet his demands for a five-year, $200 million-plus contract. The Pistons are reportedly offering around $35 million annually, leading to a significant gap in negotiations.

items.headline: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns Extension Talks Boosted by Cap Projections
items.summary: A recent $2 million increase in the NBA's 2027-28 salary-cap projections could significantly aid the New York Knicks in reaching a contract extension with Karl-Anthony Towns. This bump would allow the Knicks to offer nearly $9 million more without impacting their second apron standing.

items.headline: Al Horford Re-Signs with Golden State Warriors
items.summary: Veteran big man Al Horford declined his $5.97 million player option to sign a new two-year, $14 million deal with the Golden State Warriors. The new contract includes a second-year player option and a 15% trade kicker.

items.headline: All-Star Deni Avdija Faces Contract Issues, Injury Concerns with Trail Blazers
items.summary: Israeli forward Deni Avdija, who became the first Israeli named to an NBA All-Star Game and had a breakout 2025-26 season averaging 24.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 6.5 assists, is reportedly facing contract dilemmas due to collective bargaining agreement rules. Furthermore, Avdija was not cleared by the Portland Trail Blazers to play for Israel in FIBA World Cup qualifiers due to a complex back injury he sustained last season.
